title: Thyme — Reverse-engineering IDE
excerpt: Native desktop reverse-engineering IDE for Android apps and native binaries.
content_html:
Thyme — Native reverse-engineering IDE for macOS, Linux & Windows.

  • APK · DEX · JAR/WAR · IPA · dylib
  • A64 · A32 · T32
  • .dmg · .msi · .deb · AppImage

Open an APK and get Java back, with the symbols the compiler left behind. Open a .so and get ARM disassembly — A64, A32 or T32 — with basic blocks and control-flow graphs. Both land in one DuckDB workspace, so the call graph is a table you can run SQL against rather than a picture you have to squint at. The decompiler is linked in-process — there is no subprocess, no scratch directory, and nothing leaves the machine.

Download 49 USD one-time 490 USD one-time

Features

Java decompilation, in-process

Integrates the Garlic Java/Dex decompiler for rapid decompilation of JVM and Dalvik code, source code at github.

ARM disassembly — A64, A32 and T32

Supports static disassembly analysis for ARM A64, A32, and T32 instruction sets.

Call graph you can query

Supports call graph queries across Java, Dalvik, and native libraries, enabling seamless call graph tracing between Java and native code within APKs.

Control-flow graphs

Basic blocks with the assembly inline, edges coloured by kind, jump-to-address from the entry point table, and export to Graphviz .dot.

Hex and smali views

Drop to the byte level or to smali when the decompiler's output is not the truth you need.

Native library extraction

Pull every .so out of an APK and treat each as a project in its own right. A bare library is not a lesser project for having no Java in it.

Phone mirror

A bundled screen mirror with a GPU colour-conversion path, so a 1080×2400 device does not cost a core to watch.

MCP server

thyme --mcp speaks the Model Context Protocol over stdio, so an agent can drive the analysis. It reaches the running IDE over a unix socket or named pipe — not a network port.

AI providers, in one panel

Keep the credentials for the AI CLIs you already use in one place, and launch one against the open project.

Screenshots

Thyme with a real project open — an APK, its native libraries, and the call graph underneath. Use the arrows to page through them.

FAQ

What exactly does a licence unlock?

The Analysis pass: the workspace database, the SQL-queryable call graph, and native library analysis. Everything else — opening APK, DEX, JAR and IPA files, Java decompilation, ARM disassembly (A64, A32 and T32), hex and smali views, control-flow graphs and the phone mirror — runs without one.

Is the licence checked online?

When the licence server is reachable, yes: Thyme posts the licence to it and caches the answer locally. That is what lets a licence be revoked, and it is the only thing the app ever sends anywhere. The request contains the licence text and nothing else — no file names, no binary contents, no telemetry.

Does it work offline?

Yes. The licence is a plain text file, and the app holds the matching public key. With no network it verifies the signature locally and starts. ~/.garlic/license is the file, and it is the same file the garlic command-line tool reads, so one licence covers both.

Is my APK or binary uploaded anywhere?

No. Analysis runs entirely on your machine. The MCP server talks over a unix socket or a named pipe rather than a network port, and the only outbound request the app makes is the licence check above.

What happens after 0.1.0?

A one-time licence covers every 0.x release and the features listed above. If a future major version changes what the licence unlocks, existing licences keep working for the version they were bought on.
